project.name: Vestra
project.positioning: A standalone, modular Discord client-mod framework with a typed plugin API, settings UI, themes, patching utilities, and an installer.
project.primary_goal: Build the smallest stable client-mod runtime first, then expand through a modular plugin system.

visual_identity.logo_direction: Minimal angular V composed of two geometric cuts. Avoid Discord logo imagery.

directories.apps/installer: Install, uninstall, repair and update Vestra.
directories.packages/core: Renderer runtime, APIs, UI, plugin management and patching.
directories.packages/core/src/ui: Vestra UI components and settings pages.
directories.packages/injector: Bootstrap/injection layer that loads Vestra into Discord.
directories.packages/shared: Types, constants and utilities shared across packages.

design_principles: Every subsystem should be independently replaceable.
Plugins must not be able to crash the entire Vestra runtime.
All plugin lifecycle functions may be asynchronous.
Settings must be centralized instead of each plugin inventing storage.
Discord-specific internals must stay behind Vestra APIs where practical.
Do not implement the installer before the renderer runtime is stable.
Do not optimize for plugin quantity during early development.

lifecycle.stop: Undo plugin state, listeners, styles and patches.

settings.future_storage: native persistent configuration file through Vestra Native bridge

webpack_api.purpose: Locate Discord's internal modules without hardcoding direct bundle indexes.
requirements: Cache resolved modules where safe.
Fail gracefully if a Discord update changes a module.
Support lazy discovery.
Expose typed wrappers for commonly used modules.
Keep raw Webpack access separate from high-level APIs.

patcher.purpose: Safely intercept functions and restore them when a plugin is disabled.
requirements: Every patch returns an unpatch function.
Every patch belongs to a plugin or patch namespace.
Disabling a plugin automatically removes its patches.
A plugin failure must not permanently modify the target function.
Support multiple independent patches on the same target.

responsibilities: Opening files and folders when explicitly requested.
Safe limited access to Electron/Node functionality.
native_bridge.security_rule: Do not expose unrestricted Node or Electron access directly to arbitrary plugins.

plugin_settings_requirements: Show plugin errors without crashing settings UI.

builtin_plugins_v0.name: ImageUtilities
builtin_plugins_v0.description: Additional image-related context actions and utilities.

roadmap.name: Core Bootstrap
roadmap.deliverable: A renderer bundle can execute Vestra.start() successfully.

roadmap.name: Plugin Manager
roadmap.deliverable: Typed plugins can register, start, stop and fail safely.

roadmap.name: Settings
roadmap.deliverable: Plugin enabled state and settings persist.

roadmap.name: Styles API
roadmap.deliverable: Plugins and QuickCSS can add and remove CSS safely.

roadmap.name: Settings UI
roadmap.deliverable: Vestra settings can manage plugins and configuration.

roadmap.name: Webpack Module Finder
roadmap.deliverable: Vestra can locate internal Discord modules dynamically.

roadmap.name: Patcher
roadmap.deliverable: Plugins can patch functions with automatic cleanup.

roadmap.name: Discord Component APIs
roadmap.deliverable: Common Discord components and stores are exposed through stable wrappers.

roadmap.name: Injector
roadmap.deliverable: Vestra loads automatically into supported Discord installations.

roadmap.name: Installer
roadmap.deliverable: Users can install, uninstall and repair Vestra.

roadmap.name: Plugin Repository
roadmap.deliverable: Plugins can be discovered and managed through a repository/store system.

general: Implement only the requested subsystem in each task.
Do not rewrite unrelated working code.
Prefer small modules over giant files.
Avoid any unless there is no practical alternative.
Every disposable resource must have cleanup logic.
Every event listener created by a plugin must be removable.
Every CSS injection must be removable.
Every function patch must be reversible.
Errors from one plugin must be isolated from the rest of Vestra.
Do not silently swallow errors; send them through Vestra Logger.
Public API names should remain stable once used by built-in plugins.

requirements: TypeScript strict mode.
Plugins use definePlugin({...}).
Every plugin has name, description and authors.
Optional start() and stop().
PluginManager handles registration.
Prevent duplicate plugin names.
Enable and disable plugins.
Catch plugin exceptions so one broken plugin cannot crash Vestra.
Persist enabled states.
All lifecycle operations support async functions.
Do not implement Discord injection yet.
Do not implement Webpack patching yet.
Keep APIs modular because they will be extended later.
Create all required source files and exports.

non_goals_initially: Supporting every Discord release channel from day one.
quality_checks: Can a plugin be enabled without restarting Vestra?
Can a plugin be disabled without leaving listeners, patches or styles behind?
Does one plugin throwing an exception leave the rest of Vestra operational?
Can internal APIs change without forcing every plugin to directly depend on Discord internals?
Can the core run before the injector exists?
Are platform-specific operations isolated from renderer code?
release_0_0_1_definition_of_done: Vestra branding appears in the console and settings UI.
At least one plugin is registered.
Plugins can be enabled and disabled.
QuickCSS can inject and remove CSS.
A broken test plugin does not crash Vestra.
The project builds with zero TypeScript errors.
